Add Per-Cell QC Metrics to a Seurat Object

Source: R/diagnoseQC.R
diagnoseQC.Rd

Calculates the three per-cell metrics that single-cell filtering decisions are usually made from – mitochondrial content, ribosomal content and library complexity – and writes them into the object's metadata as pctMito, pctRibo and log10GenesPerUMI. Nothing is filtered and no cells are dropped; the metrics are added so that thresholds can be chosen by looking at the distributions first.

Usage

diagnoseQC(obj, organism = c("hsa", "mmu", "rno", "dre"), doCellCycle = FALSE)

Arguments

obj

A single Seurat object, typically the merged output of mergeSeurat(). A named list of objects is not accepted – merge it first, or lapply() over it – so that the metrics are always calculated on the same object the QC plots are drawn from.

organism

Three-letter code selecting the gene patterns: "hsa" (human, the default), "mmu" (mouse), "rno" (rat) or "dre" (zebrafish). See Gene patterns by organism.

doCellCycle

Also score cell cycle phase, by handing the annotated object to runCellCycle() with the same organism. FALSE by default: unlike the metrics above, scoring assumes normalised data, and will normalise the object itself if it arrives raw. For a non-human organism it also needs orthogene. Call runCellCycle() directly if you need its method argument.

Value

The input object with three numeric metadata columns added: pctMito, pctRibo and log10GenesPerUMI. Existing columns of the same name are overwritten, so the function is safe to re-run – with a different organism, for instance. Every other slot is untouched, and the cell count is unchanged.

With doCellCycle = TRUE, S.Score, G2M.Score and Phase are added as well – see runCellCycle() for what they mean.

Details

The two percentage metrics are computed by Seurat::PercentageFeatureSet() from organism-specific gene symbol patterns, so the object's rownames must be symbols. A matrix still keyed by Ensembl IDs will match nothing and produce columns of zeroes; that case is warned about rather than silently returned, and the warning names the pattern that failed so it is obvious what went wrong.

The metrics

pctMito

Percentage of a cell's UMIs coming from mitochondrial genes. High values mark cells that lost cytoplasmic RNA through a ruptured membrane – dying or stressed cells – and are the usual first filter. What counts as high is tissue-dependent: 5-10% is a common starting point, but cardiac, muscle and kidney samples are legitimately mitochondria-rich and a fixed cutoff will throw away real cells.

pctRibo

Percentage coming from ribosomal protein genes. Less often used as a hard filter and more often as a covariate: it varies strongly by cell type, so a sharp shift between samples that should be comparable points at a technical difference rather than a biological one.

log10GenesPerUMI

Library complexity – log10(nFeature) / log10(nCount). Falls between 0 and 1 for real cells, and low values mean a library dominated by few transcripts: ambient RNA, degraded cells, or red blood cells, which are genuinely low-complexity. Around 0.8 is a conventional floor.

The count columns the complexity metric is derived from (nCount_<assay> / nFeature_<assay>) are read from the object's default assay, so an object whose default assay is not RNA is handled without any extra argument. The three metrics themselves are always named the same way, because that is what the plotting functions look for.

Gene patterns by organism

"hsa" (human)

mito ^MT-, ribo ^RP[SL]

"mmu" (mouse)

mito ^mt, ribo ^Rp[sl]

"rno" (rat)

mito ^Mt-, ribo ^Rp[sl]

"dre" (zebrafish)

mito ^mt-, ribo ^rp[sl]

These differ only in the capitalisation convention each species' gene symbols follow, so an organism not listed here can borrow the code of one whose convention it shares.

See also

mergeSeurat(), which produces the object this expects; plotBarcodeRanks() for the other side of QC – cell calling, from the raw matrix; Seurat::PercentageFeatureSet() for the percentage calculation itself.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(path = "/path/to/Pool1/outs", multi = TRUE)
seurat      <- mergeSeurat(seurat_list)

seurat <- diagnoseQC(seurat, organism = "mmu")
head(seurat@meta.data)

# or metric-by-sample, without merging
seurat_list <- lapply(seurat_list, diagnoseQC, organism = "mmu")
} # }
